title: FTC Reports 24% Increase in Reported Fraud Losses to $15.8B
discussion_signal: The post highlights the FTC's reported-loss increase, the concentration of losses in investment and romance scams, and the distinction between reported losses and the much larger unobserved burden. Replies add concern about a possible fourth-quarter reporting dip and emphasize underreporting, turning the official series into a discussion about visibility and measurement limits.
linked_research_question: How do public discussions interpret reported fraud growth, underreporting, and possible data-quality breaks when translating administrative loss data into lived risk?
limits: Individual professional post and selected replies
Reply discussion is not a representative victim sample
Reported-loss estimates cannot establish total incidence
Public search discovery is not a platform-native Creator/API export
